svg.aria-label: What a change costs in a 30,000-app workspace: a universal-lib edit re-runs 30,708 tasks against 100 for a leaf edit; the worst case runs as one 61.2s whole-program check or a 11.0 min pipeline; and in a cross-machine observation only the pipeline ran faster on the 192-core box.
svg.text: A 30,000-app workspace: what a change actually costs
30,000 Next.js apps + 460 shared libs in one workspace — about 1.03 million generated files. Every number below was measured on this tree.
1. How far does a change reach?
5 of the libs are imported by every app. Change one and the pipeline re-runs a typecheck for every package that depends on it (plus the lib builds);
change an ordinary lib and almost nothing runs.
edit a lib EVERY app imports
the universal foundation — the worst case
30,708 tasks re-run
a typecheck per dependent package, plus the lib builds
edit an ordinary leaf lib
imported by almost nothing
100 tasks re-run
307× smaller blast radius
2. The worst case, run two ways (64-core box)
Same question — “did my change break any app?” — two mechanisms. Not like-for-like: the pipeline also builds each lib's dist output; the one command
only type-checks.
61.2s — one command
a single checker reads the whole workspace's source once
(peak RSS: 52,396MB recorded)
11.0 min — ×11 slower
standard pipeline: 30,708 tasks — a checker process
per affected package plus 460 lib builds
A breaking change is caught in 61.7s
all 30,000 affected apps flagged with exact file and line — the fix-list a codemod can consume
3. Does a bigger machine help?
The same two mechanisms on two different machines (64 vs 192 cores, recorded per run). One comparison each — a cross-machine observation, not a
controlled core-scaling experiment. The pipeline rows also differ in bun version (1.3.14 vs 1.4.2): turbo starts each task through the package
manager.
one command, 64 cores: 61.2s
one process; the smaller box was faster
one command, 192 cores: 66.6s
×1.1 slower — this check did not gain from the bigger box
pipeline, 64 cores: 11.0 min
×1.9 slower than the big box
pipeline, 192 cores: 5.8 min
ran 1.9× faster on this box (3.0× the cores)
also measured (64-core box): installing the 30,460-package workspace (plus its external deps) takes 190s (bun, warm store) · linting the whole tree takes 2.6s (oxlint)
toolchain: bun 1.3.14 (64-core) / 1.4.2 (192-core) · turbo 2.9.18 · tsgo 7.0.2 · oxlint 1.86.0 · node 22.23.3
